parentIntro: The big one — this is the exact spot the diagnostic found (she missed 42 − 27). The fix is STRATEGIES, not column sums: the jump strategy (42, jump back 20 to 22, back 2 to 20, back 5 more… 15) and counting UP to find a difference (27 to 30 is 3, 30 to 42 is 12, so 15). Draw an empty number line every single time this week.
watchFor: On things like 42 − 27 she may try digit-by-digit and hit “2 take away 7” — the moment of panic. Jump in early with the number line and ask: “would you rather jump BACK from 42, or count UP from 27?” Giving her the choice of road is half the confidence trick. Extra praise for choosing a strategy, separate from getting the answer.

demo.title: Two roads to 42 − 27
demo.say: Today umma shows you a question that looks tricky — but there are two secret roads through it, and you get to choose your favourite.

steps.caption: looks scary…
steps.say: Forty two take away twenty seven. Looks tricky! Let's draw a number line and take the first road.

steps.caption: road 1: jump back 20
steps.say: Start at forty two. Jump back twenty — that lands on twenty two.

steps.caption: then back 2, then back 5 … 15!
steps.say: Now jump back two to land on twenty, then five more. Fifteen! Forty two take away twenty seven is fifteen.

steps.caption: road 2: count UP from 27
steps.say: Here's the second road. Start at twenty seven and count UP. Three gets you to thirty, then twelve more to forty two. Three plus twelve is fifteen. Same answer, different road!

weDo.problem: 51 − 28, using jump-back on the number line.
weDo.model: Empty number line on the whiteboard. Mark 51 at the right end. She drives the jumps; you only draw what she says.
steps: Ask: “How big should the first jump back be?” (20 is friendly → lands on 31.)
“Now what?” (Back 1 to 30, then back 7 more → 23. Or back 8 in one go if she's brave.)
Ask the golden question: “Why did we jump 20 first, not 28 all at once?” (Friendly numbers first.)

weDo.problem: Harriet has 34 stickers. Ruby has 52. How many MORE does Ruby have?
weDo.model: This is a DIFFERENCE question — counting up shines here. Number line: 34 on the left, 52 on the right, find the gap.
steps: Ask: “Is anything being taken away here? Or are we finding the gap between two numbers?”
Count up together: 34 to 40 is 6. Then 40 to 52 is 12.
Add the hops: 6 + 12 = 18. Ruby has 18 more.
Name the move: “when a question says HOW MANY MORE, counting up is usually the fast road.”
